# `silk/io/logger_wasi`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A `Logger` provider for Preview 2 components whose host offers `wasi:logging`: [`WasiLogger`](#WasiLogger)
passes each message to `wasi:logging/logging.log`.

## When to use
Provide [`WasiLogger`](#WasiLogger) for `Logger` in a `wasm32-wasip2` component that runs on a platform with
a `wasi:logging` host, such as Spin or wasmCloud, so the platform collects the messages with
their level. Everywhere else, `StderrLogger` from `silk.io.logger_native` writes to standard
error, which every WASI runtime supports.

## Details
`wasi:logging` is a draft proposal, `wasi:logging@0.1.0-draft`, and not part of the command
world, so no logger uses it by default. The bundled WIT world `command` lists the interface, and
a component imports it only when it provides [`WasiLogger`](#WasiLogger). A component with its own
`[component].world` imports `wasi:logging/logging@0.1.0-draft` there.

Each call passes the level, the context given to [`WasiLogger.make`](#WasiLogger.impl.make), and the formatted message.
The logger formats into a 512-byte buffer on the stack, so a longer message is passed as several
records, in order, each ending on a whole character. The logger does not allocate.

## Errors
None. `wasi:logging` cannot refuse a message.

## Gotchas
- The provider exists only on `wasm32-wasip2`.
- A host without `wasi:logging`, such as `wasmtime run`, refuses to instantiate a component that
  uses [`WasiLogger`](#WasiLogger).
- `LogLevel.Warning` is `warn` in `wasi:logging`. Its `critical` level has no Silk level.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.logger { LogError, Logger }
import silk.io.logger_wasi { WasiLogger }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! LogError {
  let mut logger = WasiLogger.make("startup")
  let values = .{ count: 3 }

  // Logs "started 3 workers" at `info` with the context "startup".
  run Effect.logInfo("started {count} workers", &values)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Logger>(&mut logger)
  return 0
}
```

Import as `WasiLogger` with `import silk.io.logger_wasi { WasiLogger }`.

### Details

A message longer than 512 bytes is passed as several records, in order, each ending on a whole character.
